R7770.summary: Henri IV goes to Saumur to break off his sister Catherine de Bourbon's marriage to [9] (probably the Count of Soissons) and means to give her instead to [n], of whom he has great hope that he will turn Protestant; [9] is enraged.

R7771.summary: [9] is glad of the news, hoping to be no further troubled with the clamour of the Catholics.

R7772.summary: Edmondes learns secretly that Montmorency demanded, as a condition of coming, that the young Prince of Condé, heir of the crown, be delivered to Madame d'Angoulême to be brought up in his custody, popishly, as belonging to the Constable's place; the King would not assent.

R7773.summary: The King tells Edmondes 'that his faith is not vendible'.

R7774.summary: On the choice of [9] to negotiate, against the interest of [£] (probably the Duke of Guise) who seeks the government of Champagne and has renewed his intelligences in Amiens and Reims.

R7775.summary: [£2] (probably Guise) is to execute an enterprise upon Reims, which would be the carrying of the place; in clear, the King thinks of giving him the government of Provence against Épernon.

snip.cap: Stowe MS 166 f. 50 (R7770): clear English, then six lines of invented signs, to breake of the marriage betwene her and [9]

system: Graphic-sign simple substitution of English, words divided, a few homophones (d/u share a sign, a/g), single signs for persons (9, n, pound sign), inserted as runs in clear English.
